threads.body: [General] `build()` now appends every embedded `MetricDef` to the builder's shared `metricConfiguration`. Calling `build()` more than once therefore duplicates the definitions, and previously built `JmxTelemetry` instances also observe the mutation because they retain that same configuration; subsequent bean discovery can register duplicate callbacks and query each MBean multiple times. Build from a fresh combined configuration (or otherwise ensure embedded definitions are added only once).

The filter is applied only after `BeanFinder.resolveBeans()` has queried every configured ObjectName and `resolveAttributes()` has fetched MBean metadata. In v3 mode all non-JVM systems are loaded even though their unstable metrics are excluded by default, so every application repeatedly scans hundreds of disabled rules (eventually once per minute), and matching beans have their attributes inspected on every pass because enrollment never succeeds. Apply the effective filter before bean discovery, or prune disabled extractors/handlers from the configuration while retaining explicitly opted-in metrics.

replies.body: This is a known limitation of the current architecture where the metrics are not registered and polled individually. The polling is organized by mbeans rather than per-metric. Adding the ability to do so would likely require some significant refactor of the current implementation so it's probably better to do that as a later improvement.

threads.body: [General] `setServiceClassLoader` is documented as selecting the loader for SPI implementations, but this assignment also makes it the loader for bundled `jmx/rules` resources. A valid isolated SPI class loader (for example, one with no parent resources) will now make every predefined rule appear absent. Keep embedded definitions on the library's class loader and use this argument only for `ComponentLoader`, or expose a separate resource-loader API.

[Testing] `OpenFileDescriptorCount` and `MaxFileDescriptorCount` are attributes of the `java.lang:type=OperatingSystem` MBean, not `Threading`. As written, this new fixture parses successfully but can never collect either metric, so it cannot serve as a realistic unstable-rule fixture.

threads.body: An empty `IncludeExclude` is defined as carrying no configuration, but assigning it here changes this none-by-default setting to match every unstable metric. Callers that pass an empty selector (for example, after parsing an unset option) therefore opt into all experimental telemetry. Treat `isEmpty()` as no override, and update callers that intentionally want everything to use an explicit `included: "*"`.

replies.body: Yes, an empty `IncludeExclude` will include every unstable by default. This configuration is only provided to the API level and not directly to end-users, when handling the `otel.jmx.metrics.experimental.included` configuration option, the caller needs to take care to preserve the "no unstable metrics by default" behavior.

[General] This now makes `build()` fail whenever `setServiceClassLoader(...)` supplies a loader that does not expose the library's built-in Cassandra handler, even though Cassandra metrics are unstable and excluded by default. Replacement loaders are supported (the loaders in `HandlerTest` intentionally expose only their test providers), while all embedded systems are loaded unconditionally, so an unrelated custom handler can trigger this exception. Preserve the existing unresolved-handler behavior—let `BeanFinder` warn and skip it—rather than failing the whole JMX setup.
